messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@ocearahealth.com>

Cc: Legal Team <legal@ocearahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention evidence & temporary retain request

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and compliance folks kicked this into a higher priority. Two asks from Oceara:

1) For our SIG and SOC 2 evidence pack we need concrete artifacts that show how Redwood enforces data deletion for application logs and user event traces (audit trails). Examples would be: a short deletion runbook, a sample deletion job execution log, and a small sample of retained audit events with redactions.

2) For a narrow pilot (investigation of a clinical integration), we need to request a temporary retention exception for certain application logs for 12 months (we're normally at 90 days). We realize this is an exception; please confirm the approvals/process and any controls (encryption, access restrictions, retention-marker tags) you can attach.

Time is tight — can we get a first bundle by EOD Friday 6/30? Our legal cc'd here will coordinate if a formal Data Processing Schedule amendment is needed.

– Alex
Alex Porter
Head of Security Programs, Oceara Health
alex.porter@ocearahealth.com
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data retention evidence & temporary retain request

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Evelyn (Policy & Compliance) and Neha (Platform Ops) who will assemble evidence and outline the exception workflow. Quick summary of what we can provide immediately:

- Deletion runbook (PDF): how TTL-based deletions and on-demand erasure are kicked off, including KMS key lifecycle steps.
- Sample audit events (JSONL): redacted records showing deletion-job start/complete and S3 object tombstones.
- Retention matrix (CSV): per-data-type default retention, encryption-at-rest flags, and Customer Retention Tag behavior.

On the exception: we support customer-specific retention flags that pin objects for additional days and require an approval ticket + scoped IAM role for access. That said, the timeline for a change to a production TTL pipeline is typically 48–72 hours to schedule and validate (we can expedite for pilots).

Evelyn — can you confirm what legal/invoice approvals you need to sign off the 12-month pilot? Neha — can you prepare the artifacts Alex requested and include minimal access controls we would apply while logs are pinned?

I can prep a short approval template for your legal team if helpful.

Thanks,
Mike Grant
Director, Customer Security Relations
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / team — happy to coordinate approvals. A few points up front:

- Contract amendment: for a 12-month retention exception we typically require either a signed addendum (Data Processing Schedule amendment) or a written approval (email thread) that references the customer account and exact data classes. Legal, I've cc'd your contact — can you confirm preference?

- Risk/controls: we will only grant the exception to logs tagged with a customer-specific retention flag. Access will be restricted to a named role, access will go through our short-lived creds system, and all accesses will be logged into the audit stream we will share. We can also apply encryption key separation (customer-supplied KMS) for additional assurance.

- Evidence bundle: Neha, please assemble: deletion-runbook.pdf, sample-audit-events.jsonl (redacted), and the retention-matrix CSV. Include a short narrative that explains deletion triggers, TTL pipeline, and manual erase endpoints.

We will aim to deliver by EOD Fri 6/30. If legal needs a formal addendum template I can attach one by Thursday.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Policy & Compliance

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@ocearahealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 23:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention evidence & temporary retain request

Alex — delivering the initial evidence package per the asks. Attachments included: redwood-log-retention-matrix.csv, deletion-runbook.pdf, sample-audit-events.jsonl (all redacted). Quick highlights below: 

- Default behavior: application logs & user event traces are assigned a default TTL of 90 days; audit events are 365 days by default for SOC 2 purposes. Logs are garbage-collected by our TTL worker which marks objects with a tombstone and issues a KMS key rotation step prior to irreversible deletion.

- Exception workflow (how we will handle your 12-month pilot):
  * Customer request logged: create an approval ticket (we opened OCE-PR-4721).
  * Policy approval: Policy owner signs off (Evelyn).
  * Scoped retention tag applied: ops applies retention flag to only the specified log prefixes.
  * Access controls: data encrypted with either Redwood-managed keys or a customer-supplied KMS key; access limited to a named role; all accesses require MFA + short-lived session.
  * Expiry & remediation: system will automatically unenforce the retention tag at the agreed end date; we will run a verification deletion job and provide completion proof (job logs + audit event).

- Evidence notes included in attachments: sample audit events include two deletion-job pairs (start/finish), a sample S3 tombstone entry, and an access event showing role-based access to pinned logs. The deletion runbook contains the CLI commands our ops run to schedule a batch purge and the verification queries we return to customers.

Next steps for Oceara: please confirm the exact log prefixes (path patterns) you want pinned and whether you prefer Redwood-managed KMS or to provide a key. Once we have that we can schedule the change and provide the signed addendum if legal wants it.

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Platform Reliability Engineer (Ops)
Redwood Inference
